hoy.titular: Exodus day: the coaches leave for Montevideo and the Pincha hold their last session before the final

foto.alt: Estudiantes fans fill the stand at the UNO.

hoy.resumen: The official coaches leave the UNO at 7am and around 35,000 Pincha fans are expected in Uruguay. The squad hold their last session today at Montevideo City Torque's complex and Medina settles the line-up for Saturday's final against Palmeiras.

siete.titulo: Club coaches leave the UNO today at 7am
siete.texto: The official coaches leave the UNO today at 7am (check-in from 5.30am) and the supporters' groups' coaches at midday, to speed up the border crossing. A physical ID card or valid passport is required: the Mi Argentina digital ID is not accepted.

More than 170 fans' coaches will pass through Gualeguaychú on the way to the bridge, others crossed by Buquebus ferry and even on three sailing boats from Ensenada. The media estimate around 35,000 Pincha fans in Montevideo for the final.

siete.titulo: Piovi: "We will go on the attack"
siete.texto: After the first session in Montevideo, Ezequiel Piovi said the squad have already studied Palmeiras and warned: "On Saturday we will go on the attack, as we have done so far". For him, it is the biggest match of his career.
The squad train today from 10am at Montevideo City Torque's complex in Ciudad de la Costa, in the last session before the final. As all week, with no press or public.

siete.titulo: Andújar and Boselli to walk out with the Cup
siete.texto: Two 2009 champions will carry the trophy onto the Centenario pitch minutes before kick-off: Mariano Andújar, that campaign's record-breaking goalkeeper, and Mauro Boselli, its top scorer with 8 goals.

Fabricio Pérez is the front-runner to replace the suspended Baltasar Rodríguez, with Cetré as the alternative; Medina also tried a back five with Gastón Benedetti. Correa travelled among the 27 in the squad but still has no confirmed medical clearance.

siete.titulo: Abel praises the Pincha, Barboza talks big
siete.texto: Abel Ferreira praised the Pincha: "They are an extremely competitive side, with very experienced players". More provocatively, Argentine defender Alexander Barboza said he will win the final "in his other home, Uruguay". Paulinho, injured since October, remains a doubt.
